title: Positive scaling preserves threshold signs
statement: Let $c,r\in\mathbb R$ with $c>0$, and define $sigma(t)=1$ when $t\ge0$ and $sigma(t)=-1$ when $t<0$. Then $sigma(cr)=sigma(r)$.
replaced:
Let $c,r\in\mathbb R$ with $c>0$, and define $\sigma(t)=1$ when $t\ge0$ and
$\sigma(t)=-1$ when $t<0$.
Then $\sigma(cr)=\sigma(r)$.
